summary: Lambert Schmithausen worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Erich Frauwallner (~1959–1963) and Paul Hacker (~1963–1966). He served as an associate professor at the University of Münster (1970–1973) and on the Advisory Board at the University of Hamburg (1973–2005).

Lance E. Nelson specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at McMaster University in 1986 and held a post as a professor at the University of San Diego (attested 1997).

Lance S. Cousins worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey, Boonman Poonyathiro, and K. R. Norman. He held posts at Manchester, Oxford, and Wolfson College, and was President of the Pali Text Society (2002–2003).
Lang Chen works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD at Yale University, where she studied under Janet Gyatso, Koichi Shinohara, and Phyllis Granoff.

Lang Eun Ra is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She was a doctoral student at Temple University, where she was supervised by Charles Wei-hsun Fu and studied under Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert M. Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler.

Lara Braitstein specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and serves there as Associate Professor of Indo-Tibetan Buddhism (attested 2026).

Larry DeVries is an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Minnesota. He held teaching posts at Minnesota, Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Washington, a research position at Chicago, and was attested at Langara College in 2005.

Lars Fogelin works in history and archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (1995–2003) under Carla Sinopoli and held posts at Albion College, Southern Illinois University Carbondale, and the University of Arizona.

Lars Martin Fosse works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Oslo (~1971–1994), Heidelberg University, and the University of Bonn, and taught at the University of Oslo (attested 2002).

Lata Chhatre specializes in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She has held posts at Savitribai Phule Pune University as Reader in the Department of Philosophy (attested 2009) and as Visiting Faculty (attested 2026).

Lata Deokar works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She served as a Research Assistant at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2001–2004) and as Visiting Faculty at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 2026).

Lata S. Bapat works in philosophy and Indology. She completed her PhD under M. P. Marathe at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1985, where she also served as a Research Associate in Buddhist Philosophy (attested 1989).

Lati Rinpoche was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who earned his Geshe Lharampa at Ganden Shartse Monastery and studied at Gyuto Monastery. He served as Abbot of Ganden Shartse Monastery (~1976–1984) and visited the University of Virginia (1976).

Latika Lahiri is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji as an Indian Government scholar in 1958 and later held a post at the University of Delhi.

Laura Harrington is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University under Ryuichi Abe, Theodore Riccardi Jr., Gary A. Tubb, Lobsang Jamspal, Kirti Rinpoche, Tenzin Norbu, Nathaniel Dickson, and Gregory Hillis.

Lauran R. Hartley specializes in Tibetology. She held positions at Indiana University Bloomington, Rutgers University (attested 2003), and Latse Library (attested 2003), and serves as Adjunct Assistant Professor and Director of the Modern Tibetan Studies Program at Columbia University (attested 2026).

Laurence Austine Waddell was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology who earned a medical degree from the University of Glasgow. He served in the Indian Medical Service and Indian Army, and was Professor of Tibetan at University College London (1906–1908).

Laurence Binyon worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology after studying at Trinity College, Oxford. He spent his career primarily at the British Museum (~1893–1933) and held a post at Harvard University (~1933–1934).

Laurence Khantipalo Mills worked in Buddhist studies. He studied under Acharya Buddharakkhita, Sangharakshita, Chien Ming Chen, Dhardo Rinpoche, Namkhai Norbu, and Dudjom Rinpoche, and served as abbot at Wat Buddha Dhamma in 1978.

Laurie L. Patton works in Indology and religious studies. She earned degrees from Harvard and the University of Chicago, held professorships at Emory (~1996–2011) and Duke (~2011–2015), and served as President of Middlebury College (2015–2024) and the American Academy of Arts and Sciences (~2023).
